title: Pre-signed URLs are signed with a key that may be empty, so 'signed' means 'anyone can sign it' for any user
index_line: T-0091 · AUTH_DECISION · pre-signed WebDAV URL with an empty per-user signing key: forge the signature for any victim · php · corroborated
invariant_violated: The pre-signed URL scheme assumed a per-instance signing key exists and is secret: possession of a valid signature therefore proves the issuer authorised the access. When no key is configured the secret is empty, so the signature is a computation anyone can perform — the check still runs, and still passes, for a caller who was never authorised.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated request arrives at a WebDAV/pre-signed URL naming a victim username
the server derives the signing key for that owner's files; with none configured it uses an empty secret
the supplied signature is verified as an HMAC over the URL with that key
the comparison succeeds because the key is empty and computable, not because the caller is authorised
the request proceeds under the victim's identity
the caller reads, modifies or deletes any file as that user without authentication

source.http.request.value: the WebDAV/pre-signed URL: username plus signature as query parameters, no session

guard.signature.value: the HMAC check whose key is empty when no signing key is configured

sink.file.read.value: the file operation performed as the victim user once the check passes

encoding.string.value: the signature is a computable string over public inputs, so an empty key makes it forgeable

preconditions.expr: the ownCloud instance exposes WebDAV and pre-signed URLs
the pre-signed URL code path signs with a possibly-empty key

success: a URL with a signature computed over an empty key returns file contents for a user the tester never authenticated as
the same forged URL can modify or delete a file
failure_like: pre-signed URLs are refused when no signing key is configured (10.13.1+ behaviour)
the instance has a key configured, so the signature cannot be computed
false_positive: a public share link is meant to be unauthenticated — require access to a victim-owned file outside any share
a 401/403 with a signature error is the check working

hazards: every 'signed URL' design: the signature's meaning collapses when the key is absent, default, or globally shared
the username is part of the signed material, so knowing a username is the only prerequisite
'configured in production' is not a security control — a default install is the target
non_transfers: implementations that refuse to issue or accept pre-signed URLs without a non-empty key
per-user keys derived from a server secret that always exists

evidence.target: ownCloud core before 10.13.1, WebDAV pre-signed URL authentication (CVE-2023-49105)

provenance.author: ownCloud (security advisory)
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2023-49105: it is possible to access, modify or delete any file without authentication if the username of the victim is known; the fix denies pre-signed URLs when no signing key is configured for the owner of the files

provenance.author: Hunt.io (Attack Capture)
provenance.corroborates: in-the-wild use: scripts targeted an ownCloud instance using pre-signed URLs generated with an empty signing secret, allowing unauthenticated retrieval of files over WebDAV; the operator even hosted a local ownCloud to test the technique
